items.reason: A bridge is an edge whose deletion adds a component; it is a connectivity notion, not a plane-graph one. Its deps are def-graph-deletion-contraction-minor-and-subdivision, def-connected-graph-and-connected-component and cor-connected-components-partition-the-vertex-set, all on graphs-walks-and-connectivity (order 207). Placed immediately after def-vertex-and-edge-connectivity, since a bridge is exactly a cut edge. Ear decompositions and flow theory need it here.

The characterisation belongs with the definition it characterises. Its remaining deps (def-graph-walk-trail-path-and-cycle, def-connected-graph-and-connected-component, def-graph-deletion-contraction-minor-and-subdivision) are all on the receiving page.

Its two substantive deps, cor-whitney-k-connected-path-characterisation and thm-menger-finite-directed-and-undirected-path-forms, are the last two items of matchings-covers-menger-and-network-flows (order 213); def-finite-cardinality resolves at order 20. It is a connectivity result used by, not derived from, planarity. Appended after the Whitney corollary it uses.

A Kempe chain is a component of the subgraph induced by two colour classes, defined for any proper colouring; nothing in it mentions the plane. Deps are def-proper-vertex-colouring-and-chromatic-number (graph-colouring, order 215), def-subgraph-induced-subgraph-and-spanning-subgraph and def-connected-graph-and-connected-component (order 207). Vizing's fan argument and Brooks-style recolouring cannot reach it at order 357.

The swap lemma is the operative half of the Kempe device and travels with the definition. Its deps beyond def-kempe-chain are def-proper-vertex-colouring-and-chromatic-number and def-connected-graph-and-connected-component, both at or below order 215.
